page0.text:
"Ungh!"
I desperately parry the constant flurry of fists.
Kuzuki's fists are live "snakes." Even if I barely dodge them, they change their course of direction to come bite me the moment I avoid them.
That's how Saber got seriously injured.
Saber was grazed by Kuzuki's "snake" because she had the reflexes to dodge it.

page1.text:
But, I don't have such reflexes.
I can't dodge them, and first of all, I can't even see his fists.
I can't see them, so it's impossible to even dodge them.

page2.text:
"Guh...!"
My shoulder. Kuzuki's fist grazes my left collarbone.
"Haah, guh...!"
It's like a sledgehammer. It feels as if my left shoulder is shattered and I almost drop my dagger.

page3.text:
"...Ungh."
I stop and bear it, repelling the repeated fists aiming towards my face with the dagger in my right hand.

page4.text:
"Agh, guh...!"
I desperately retreat.
I retreat without regard for my appearance, while Kuzuki closes in, without revealing how he advanced.

page5.text:
"Haah..."
I shiver at his stance.
I won't be able to withstand the next attack.
It's absurd that I was able to parry all the attacks until now.
It doesn't feel real. My misunderstanding of being able to manage with just defense and being a decoy until Tohsaka defeats Caster shattered from the first blow.

page6.text:
Souichirou Kuzuki took our previous battle in account.
Before, I was able to fend off Kuzuki, who attacked Tohsaka.
So I thought I'd be able to block his attacks if I Projected Archer's twin swords.
But.
On the other hand, that means I can't do anything without Archer's swords.

page7.text:
Kuzuki took that into consideration.
This time, the first thing that Kuzuki did was try to take away my twin swords.

page8.text:
"Guh...!"
My right dagger shatters.
His fist, Strengthened by Caster's magecraft, destroys my sword with just a few blows.

page9.text:
"Trace, on...!"
I immediately replace the dagger.
I can't expect high quality from a forced Projection and quickly made swords.
As a result, the twin swords that had received several attacks lose their accuracy.

page10.text:
"Guh... Haah, haah, haah...!"
I can't control my breathing.
I frantically block Kuzuki's snake with my twin swords.
My body just follows the twin swords. My limbs that copy Archer's movements have far exceeded the limits of my body.

page11.text:
And then there's this headache.
My body erodes every time my twin swords are destroyed and I Project new ones.
It's different from using up magical energy.
It feels like I lose one of the few Magic Circuits I have every time I make a new sword.

page12.text:
I'm almost out.
I might be able to make two more.
It's over when my magical energy runs out.
But, first of all...
Would I even be able to make two more...?

page13.text:
"Huh... uh?"
I'm in the air.
Kuzuki's right fist. The fist that he hadn't been using was thrust like a spear.

page14.text:
I parried the blow that tried to pierce through my chest and rib cage with my twin swords.
In an instant, my twin swords are destroyed, and it seems like I was flung away from the impact.
I feel something hard against my back.
...I must've been flung about five meters.

page15.text:
"Haah... Guh."
I try to resume my breathing and realize I can't breathe.
The penetrating impact is numbing my heart.
I can't breathe, and I can't even move my limbs.
Just for a few seconds.
During that gap of my heart resuming to work,

page16.text:
"Hnng..."
the devil approaches.
This is it.
This man would finish me off if I dropped my guard for only a second.
With me like this, it would be more than enough time to kill me six times.

page17.text:
...
I glare at my enemy.
Even if my limbs don't move, there are still things I can do.
I'm not one who wields swords to start with.
My weapon that I fight with has always been magecraft.
Then... It's not over yet.
My role is to hold Kuzuki down. I can't give up without fulfilling my role...!

page18.text:
"Huh?"
...
That hitting sound didn't come from in front of me.
The structure of the sword that I was imagining disappears.
Kuzuki, who was approaching to twist off my neck, stops.
That abnormality was behind Kuzuki.
It happened to Caster, with the altar behind her.

page19.text:
Tohsaka is also at an advantage.
No, the burden is greater than mine since she clearly understands the difference in their powers.

page20.text:
"——"
Caster points her fingers towards her, full of composure.
The magecraft is "Aero."
Caster has no need for incantations.
To the witch that lived in the age of gods, she does not need a process to connect herself with the world.
Caster is always surrounded by the divine mysteries that make the world go round.
For her, magecraft is just something she commands.
It is just like ordering a guard dog to attack.

page21.text:
"...Acht (Eighth)...!"
She counters that with her treasured jewels.
She does not have the time to cast a spell, and she cannot match Caster's magecraft with simple spells.

page22.text:
Their skills as a mage are as far apart as heaven and earth.
To bridge that gap, she can only bring out the thing that she has been accumulating for a long time.
The crystallization of magical energy that she has stored since she was born as the daughter of a mage.
She faces the challenge, preparing to use the remaining nine out of ten irreplaceable jewels.

page23.text:
"Heheh, how brave of you. I didn't think you had such a trump card, young lady."
Caster keeps her smile, even though her magecraft is being nullified by pure magical energy.

page24.text:
Caster, who can exercise magecraft almost infinitely,
and the girl who opposes her using jewels as amplifiers.
That difference is obvious.
I do not know how many jewels she has, but it should be around ten or twenty.
There is no way she can defeat Caster with that amount.

page25.text:
"...Sieben (Seventh)...!"
She neutralizes the electric charge with the seventh jewel.
There are six jewels left.
With six more spells from Caster, her trump card will run out.

page26.text:
"Oh, you dodge them well. So brave. You wouldn't run out of jewels if you were just protecting yourself."
Without reacting to the giggling voice, she readies the jewel between her fingers in preparation for the next bullet.
...Just as Caster says, her jewels would not shatter if she were just protecting herself.
Each jewel should be able to block Caster's spell about three times.

page27.text:
...But, she couldn't do that.
Caster's magecraft covers the sanctuary once it is activated.
Kuzuki should be protected by Caster, but he is an exception.
If she doesn't counter Caster's magecraft before it is activated, then Shirou Emiya, who is keeping Souichirou Kuzuki busy, will burn and die.

page28.text:
"...Ungh."
Therefore, it is meaningless if she protects only herself.
She can't let him die like that, and the premise of this strategy is that he stops Kuzuki.

page29.text:
"Oh, you still plan to keep on protecting him? That is quite some conviction, but I wonder how long that will last. The result is clear if all you do is defend, young lady."
Caster's fingers move.

page30.text:
"...Sechs (Sixth) Ein Fluß, ein Halt (Winter River)...!"
In response to that, she makes the first move.
Her jewels will run out and she will be killed if she keeps on defending.
Caster's magecraft and her jewels.
If the magical energy contained is the same, then it means she can beat Caster if she makes the first move...!

page31.text:
"——"
But, she cannot surpass Caster's spells.
If Rin Tohsaka is the fastest without using spells and can establish magecraft just by releasing jewels,
Caster is also the fastest as she can create divine mysteries with just one phrase.
There is no first move in their battle.
This is just a clash of power against power.
The first one to lose from the clash and run out of magical energy loses.
Then...

page33.text:
But the witch in purple blocks it like it is nothing.
No, it wasn't just that...
Caster had swallowed all of her magical energy into her robe.

page34.text:
...
Tohsaka stands there in astonishment.
...Behind her, she can hear the sound of his defeat.
The sound of breaking swords and his body slamming against the wall.

page35.text:
The match is about to be settled.
There is nothing she can do, and her body sways.
She staggers forward as if defeated by inescapable despair.

page36.text:
"Oh, this is it? You still have more jewels, right? Why don't you try until you run out without giving up?"
...
She has no energy to answer.
...Regardless of how many jewels she has left, this was the best she could do.
If that didn't work, not even a hundred jewels would be enough to hurt Caster with her magecraft...

page37.text:
"I see. It seems you finally realized that you're no match for me no matter what you do. But it was fun, young lady. It has been a while since I competed with magecraft.
Yes, I shall give you value just because of that."
"Guh...!"
She stops herself from falling forward, suppresses her nausea with her hand, and keeps glaring at Caster.

page38.text:
"Is it vexing? But this is reality. Actually, you should be proud.
Even though I did play with you, you forced me to compete in magecraft."
Then Caster points at her.
As if to pronounce her death sentence.
"Disappear. It is a matter of time until that boy is defeated by my Master.
Before that...let us finish as well."
Caster slowly murmurs her death.
That opening.
She had been waiting for that judgment.
"Stark (Second)—Groß (Strengthen) zwei"
She only needs one phrase to release the spell.
She hangs her head and smiles as she murmurs.

page40.text:
I doubt my own eyes for a moment.
Tohsaka and Caster.
Their battle of magecraft ended with Tohsaka's defeat.
Tohsaka slowly staggered forward as if asking for Caster's forgiveness, and Caster released magecraft to finish her off.

page41.text:
That... moment...
Tohsaka counters the released magecraft.

page42.text:
That's fine.
That's not surprising.
The problem is after that... Tohsaka punches Caster with a fired up stance...!

page43.text:
Tohsaka throws herself into the hellfire.
She counters the released magecraft and, using it as a distraction, she jumps onto Caster.

page44.text:
"...Guh!?"
Caster's surprise is that of a mage.
She could not have predicted that the mage that lost in magecraft would come punching at her.
I didn't expect it either, so it must be like blasphemy for Caster, who is an excellent mage.

page45.text:
But, that isn't just a useless struggle.
Tohsaka closes in and lands a one-inch punch, a Chinese martial arts move, on Caster's chest.

page46.text:
"Guh... Ugh...!?"
A shattering sound.
Tohsaka must've Strengthened her fist like Kuzuki, as her blow easily breaks through Caster's defense.

page47.text:
"...You're a mage and you're fighting bare-handed...!?"
"Tough luck...! Self-defense is a required subject for mages nowadays...!"

page48.text:
"..."
I'm honestly fascinated by her coordination.
Tohsaka drops to the ground right after the one-inch punch.
Putting both hands on the ground, she crouches down to Caster's knees.
To Caster, who has no hand-to-hand combat knowledge, it must look like Tohsaka disappeared.
Then, she executes a foot sweep.
Her kick using her entire body is explosive, as if trying to kick off Caster's legs.

page49.text:
"Ah...!?"
Caster's feet are swept beneath her and lands on her back.

page50.text:
But it doesn't stop.
After the sweep, Tohsaka stands up with her back turned to Caster, uses the turning momentum to jab Caster with an elbow...
"Fly...!"
Tohsaka stops her turning and throws a straight punch at Caster, putting her weight into it...!

page51.text:
"Guh...!"
Caster's body is blown away.
Taking Tohsaka's straight punch directly, Caster is slammed into the wall like me.

page52.text:
"Ah... Agh!"
Leaning against the wall, Caster pants dizzily.

page53.text:
"Got you...!"
There is distance between them.
Tohsaka kicks the ground to cover the few meters between them.
The match is settled.
Caster cannot move, and her wound seems fatal.

page54.text:
The battle only lasted for a few seconds.
The match is settled within a five second interval after I was smashed into the wall when confronting Kuzuki.

page55.text:
Caster has no energy left to fight back.
Tohsaka closes in on Caster with Saber-like speed and delivers the finishing blow.

page56.text:
Strengthening for just a few seconds using magecraft.
Tohsaka intended to fight Caster close combat from the start.
Caster only saw Tohsaka as a mage.
She acted like she was at a disadvantage so that she could use that opening to achieve her one-time surprise attack.

page57.text:
And the plan worked.
Caster was deceived by Tohsaka and completely lost.
Tohsaka has won this battle.
Yes.
"...No. That's far enough, Tohsaka."
If not for this man's monstrous athleticism.

page58.text: If Tohsaka running to Caster was like a hurricane, then his speed is like a storm caused by the devil.

page59.text:
"No... way..."
Tohsaka stops.
In front of Caster leaning against the wall is Souichirou Kuzuki, who was just in front of me until now.

page60.text:
"Oh..."
Tohsaka moves.
The instant Tohsaka feels death and immediately shields her face while jumping back,
Kuzuki's right fist that blew me away strikes Tohsaka's face.

page61.text:
"Ungh...!"
Tohsaka guards her face with both hands and jumped back, but she's sent flying.
Tohsaka is smashed into the wall opposite from me with her arms dangling down, as if they are broken.

page62.text:
"You missed your chance of victory. It's because of your inexperience that you weren't able to kill her after four strikes."
He says calmly.
...But, that's not Tohsaka's fault.
The reason she lost her chance is because of me.
If I had stopped Kuzuki, Tohsaka would have defeated Caster.
